paragraphs.title: Eating the Scroll and Accepting the Mission

easy.explanation: The LORD commanded Ezekiel to eat the scroll.
easy.q: What did the LORD command Ezekiel to do with the scroll?

easy.explanation: Ezekiel was sent to speak to the house of Israel.
easy.q: To whom was Ezekiel sent to speak?

easy.explanation: The scroll was in his mouth as honey for sweetness.
easy.q: How did the scroll taste in Ezekiel's mouth?

answers: He received and internalized God's message
medium.explanation: Eating the scroll represents receiving God's words inwardly.
medium.q: What does Ezekiel's eating the scroll before his mission suggest?

answers: Went to speak to the house of Israel
medium.explanation: After eating the scroll, he was sent to speak to Israel.
medium.q: What did Ezekiel do after eating the scroll?

answers: Take God's message deeply within himself
medium.explanation: The words describe inwardly receiving the message of the scroll.
medium.q: What does “cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roll” mean in context?

answers: The messenger must first receive the message within himself
The messenger may change the message
The messenger need not understand the message
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel eats the scroll before he is sent to speak God's words.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between eating the scroll and Ezekiel's mission?

answers: The scroll contained only words of comfort
Receiving God's word is presented as sweet
Israel had already accepted God's word
challenge.explanation: The passage says the scroll was sweet, but it does not say its contents were only comforting.
challenge.q: What may be understood from the scroll being sweet even though it was given to the house of Israel?

answers: Opening his mouth and eating the scroll
The command to go and speak
challenge.explanation: The command to go and speak moves Ezekiel from receiving the message to proclaiming it.
challenge.q: Which action shows the movement from receiving the message to carrying out the mission?

paragraphs.title: A Mission to a People Who Refuse to Listen

easy.explanation: He was sent to the house of Israel, not to a people of a strange speech.
easy.q: Was Ezekiel sent to a people with a strange speech?

easy.explanation: The house of Israel is described as impudent and hardhearted.
easy.q: How is the house of Israel described?

answers: A strong face and a strong forehead
easy.explanation: The LORD made Ezekiel's face and forehead strong against theirs.
easy.q: What did the LORD give Ezekiel against the people?

answers: He did not know the people's language
The people were stubborn and would not listen
He had not received God's words
medium.explanation: The difficulty was the people's refusal to listen, not a language barrier.
medium.q: Why might Ezekiel have found his mission difficult?

medium.explanation: The expression describes firmness against opposition and rebellion.
medium.q: What does “an hard forehead” suggest in this passage?

medium.explanation: He was to speak to them and tell them what the Lord God said.
medium.q: What was Ezekiel commanded to do even if the people would not listen?

challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that Israel would not hearken because it was rebellious.
challenge.q: What is the main source of difficulty in Ezekiel's mission?

answers: So he would not be afraid of the people's opposition
So he could lead an army
So he would not need to speak
challenge.explanation: The LORD strengthened him so he would not fear or be dismayed by the rebellious people.
challenge.q: Why did the LORD strengthen Ezekiel's face and forehead?

answers: Ezekiel could choose whether to speak
The mission depended on the people's response
Ezekiel had to deliver the message without controlling their response
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel was responsible to speak, but the people chose whether to hear or refuse.
challenge.q: What does “whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear” mean?

paragraphs.title: The Spirit Carries Ezekiel to the Exiles

easy.explanation: The spirit lifted Ezekiel up and carried him away.

answers: A voice of a great rushing
easy.explanation: He heard a voice of a great rushing behind him.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel hear behind him?

easy.explanation: He remained among them astonished for seven days.
easy.q: How many days did Ezekiel sit among the exiles in astonishment?

answers: The noise of the wings of the living creatures and the wheels
Only the sound of the river
medium.explanation: He heard the wings of the living creatures, the wheels, and a great rushing.
medium.q: What sounds were included in the noise Ezekiel heard?

answers: The spirit lifted him up and took him away
medium.explanation: The spirit lifted him up and took him away.
medium.q: How did Ezekiel come to the exiles?

medium.explanation: The word describes a state of amazement and shock.
medium.q: What does “astonished” describe in Ezekiel's condition?

answers: He moved from an overwhelming experience to astonishment
He decided never to speak again
challenge.explanation: The powerful sound and movement were followed by his sitting astonished among the exiles.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the movement from the great rushing to Ezekiel's silent sitting?

challenge.explanation: The expression describes Ezekiel's troubled and intense inner state.
challenge.q: What does “I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit” describe?

answers: He remained astonished for seven days
He spoke immediately to the people
challenge.explanation: Remaining astonished for seven days shows the powerful effect of the experience.
challenge.q: Which detail most emphasizes the intensity of Ezekiel's experience?

paragraphs.title: The Prophet as Watchman and the Duty to Warn

answers: A watchman to the house of Israel
easy.explanation: The LORD appointed Ezekiel as a watchman to the house of Israel.
easy.q: What did the LORD appoint Ezekiel to be?

answers: Both the wicked and the righteous
easy.explanation: The passage gives Ezekiel duties concerning both wicked and righteous people.
easy.q: Whom was Ezekiel required to warn?

answers: The wicked person dies in his iniquity, but Ezekiel delivers his soul
The wicked person immediately becomes righteous
Ezekiel is punished for warning him
easy.explanation: The wicked person dies in his iniquity, but Ezekiel has delivered his soul.
easy.q: What happens if Ezekiel warns the wicked person, but that person does not turn?

medium.explanation: His responsibility was to hear God's word and give the people warning.
medium.q: What was Ezekiel's chief responsibility as a watchman?

answers: He lives because of his former righteousness
He dies in his sin, and his blood is required from the watchman
medium.explanation: The passage says he dies in his sin and his blood is required from Ezekiel.
medium.q: What happens if a righteous man turns from righteousness and is not warned?

answers: One who recognizes danger and warns others
medium.explanation: A watchman is responsible for seeing danger and warning the people.
medium.q: What does “watchman” mean in this context?

answers: The prophet is responsible to deliver the warning
The prophet decides whether the person will live
People are not responsible for their actions
challenge.explanation: In both cases Ezekiel must warn, while the person's response remains his own responsibility.
challenge.q: What principle is shared by the warning of the wicked and the warning of the righteous?

answers: He must warn the person without ceasing
challenge.explanation: When the warning is given, Ezekiel has delivered his soul even if the person does not turn.
challenge.q: What happens to Ezekiel when he warns someone who does not change?

answers: A righteous man who turns to sin must also be warned
challenge.explanation: The passage says that even a righteous man must be warned if he turns to sin.
challenge.q: What distinction does the passage make concerning the righteous?

paragraphs.title: The Valley, the Glory of God, and Seclusion

easy.explanation: The LORD told Ezekiel to arise and go forth into the plain.
easy.q: Where did the LORD command Ezekiel to go?

easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw the glory of the LORD standing there.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel see in the plain?

easy.explanation: The LORD told him to shut himself within his house.
easy.q: What did the LORD later command Ezekiel to do?

answers: Like the glory he saw by the river of Chebar
Like the rushing sound among the exiles
medium.explanation: It was like the glory he had seen by the river of Chebar.
medium.q: What was the glory of the LORD like when Ezekiel saw it in the plain?

answers: It set him upon his feet
It caused him to fall asleep
It returned him to the exiles
medium.explanation: The spirit entered him and set him upon his feet.
medium.q: What happened when the spirit entered Ezekiel?

answers: Ezekiel went out to the people
medium.explanation: The bands represented a restriction on Ezekiel's movement.
medium.q: What does being bound with bands indicate in this passage?

answers: Seclusion, seeing the glory, then going to the plain
Going to the plain, seeing the glory, then shutting himself in the house
Seeing the glory, eating the scroll, then going to the plain
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel went to the plain, saw the glory of the LORD, and was then commanded to shut himself in his house.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events?

answers: He had complete freedom of action
His mission included a period of seclusion and limitation
He was no longer a prophet
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly describes bands, seclusion, and restricted movement.
challenge.q: What does the restriction of Ezekiel's movement show?

answers: His silence was part of the LORD's control over the delivery of the message
The people had already listened to everything
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel's speech would be opened by the LORD at the appointed time, even though the people were rebellious.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the restriction of Ezekiel's speech and the rebelliousness of the people?

paragraphs.title: The Opening of the Mouth and the Final Message

answers: When the LORD spoke with him
easy.explanation: The LORD would open Ezekiel's mouth when He spoke with him.
easy.q: When would the LORD open Ezekiel's mouth?

answers: The words of the king of Israel
easy.explanation: Ezekiel would say, “Thus saith the Lord God.”
easy.q: What would Ezekiel say when his mouth was opened?

easy.explanation: The people are described as a rebellious house.
easy.q: How is the people described at the end of the verse?

answers: Some would hear and some would refuse
medium.explanation: The verse says, “He that heareth, let him hear; and he that forbeareth, let him forbear.”
medium.q: What would be the responses of those who heard the message?

answers: He delivered God's words rather than a private message of his own
He chose the content of the prophecy
He did not need to speak
medium.explanation: His opened mouth was for declaring the words given by the Lord God.
medium.q: What does the opening of Ezekiel's mouth teach about his role?

answers: The one who refuses may continue to refuse
The one who listens will be punished
The one who speaks will become a prophet
medium.explanation: The expression allows the one who refuses to continue refusing the message.
medium.q: What does “he that forbeareth, let him forbear” mean?

answers: In both places he must deliver God's words to the house of Israel
At the beginning he was forbidden to speak
At the end he was sent to foreign nations
challenge.explanation: Both the beginning and the end emphasize Ezekiel's mission to speak God's words to Israel.
challenge.q: How does the final message connect with the mission given to Ezekiel at the beginning of the chapter?

answers: The hearers remain responsible for their response
There is no need to deliver the warning
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel delivers the message, while the hearers choose whether to listen or refuse.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by “he that heareth, let him hear; and he that forbeareth, let him forbear”?

answers: His speech depended on the LORD's command, not merely on his own will
He permanently lost the ability to speak
He was allowed to speak only about himself
challenge.explanation: The passage says the LORD would open his mouth when He spoke with Ezekiel.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Ezekiel's silence before his mouth was opened and the final message?
